arxiv-1808-10617.title: Gradual Collective Upgrade of a Swarm of Autonomous Buoys for Dynamic Ocean Monitoring
arxiv-1808-10617.creator: Francesco Vallegra, David Mateo, Grgur Tokić, Roland Bouffanais, Dick K. P. Yue
arxiv-1808-10617.description: Abstract Swarms of autonomous surface vehicles equipped with environmental sensors and decentralized communications bring a new wave of attractive possibilities for the monitoring of dynamic features in oceans and other waterbodies. However, a key challenge in swarm robotics design is the efficient collective operation of heterogeneous systems.

arxiv-2107-12829.title: Conflict-Free Four-Dimensional Path Planning for Urban Air Mobility Considering Airspace Occupations Journal: XXX
arxiv-2107-12829.creator: Wei Dai, Bizhao Pang, Kin Huat Low
arxiv-2107-12829.description: Abstract Urban air mobility (UAM) has attracted the attention of aircraft manufacturers, air navigation service providers and governments in recent years. Preventing the conflict among urban aircraft is crucial to UAM traffic safety, which is a key in enabling large scale UAM operation.

While LLMs have made it possible to rapidly prototype new ML functionalities, many real-world applications involve complex tasks that cannot be easily handled via a single run of an LLM.

arxiv-2211-12823.title: Quasinormal mode representation of radiating resonators in open phononic systems
arxiv-2211-12823.creator: Vincent Laude, Yan-Feng Wang
arxiv-2211-12823.description: Abstract Open phononic systems including resonators radiating inside an unbounded medium support localized phonons characterized by a complex frequency. In this context, the concept of elastic quasinormal mode (QNM) arises naturally, as in the cases of nanophotonic and plasmonic open systems.

arxiv-2302-14235.title: Ntuple Wizard: An Application to Access Large-Scale Open Data from LHCb
arxiv-2302-14235.creator: Christine A. Aidala, Christopher Burr, Marco Cattaneo, Dillon S. Fitzgerald, Adam Morris, Sebastian Neubert, Donijor Tropmann
arxiv-2302-14235.description: Abstract Making the large data sets collected at the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) accessible to the world is a considerable challenge because of both the complexity and the volume of data. This paper presents the Ntuple Wizard, an application that leverages the existing computing infrastructure available to the LHCb collaboration in order to enable third-party users to request specific data.

arxiv-2402-12960.title: Inferring Non-Failure Conditions for Declarative Programs
arxiv-2402-12960.creator: Michael Hanus
arxiv-2402-12960.description: Abstract Unintended failures during a computation are painful but frequent during software development. Failures due to external reasons (e.g., missing files, no permissions) can be caught by exception handlers. Programming failures, such as calling a partially defined operation with unintended arguments, are often not caught due to the assumption that the software is correct.

arxiv-2404-14340.title: Hybrid Intersection Types for PCF (Extended Version)
arxiv-2404-14340.creator: Pablo Barenbaum, Delia Kesner, Mariana Milicich
arxiv-2404-14340.description: Abstract Intersection type systems have been independently applied to different evaluation strategies, such as call-by-name (CBN) and call-by-value (CBV). These type systems have been then generalized to different subsuming paradigms being able, in particular, to encode CBN and CBV in a unique unifying framework.

arxiv-2410-07567.title: When and Where Did it Happen? An Encoder-Decoder Model to Identify Scenario Context
arxiv-2410-07567.creator: Enrique Noriega-Atala, Robert Vacareanu, Salena Torres Ashton, Adarsh Pyarelal, Clayton T. Morrison, Mihai Surdeanu
arxiv-2410-07567.description: Abstract We introduce a neural architecture finetuned for the task of scenario context generation: The relevant location and time of an event or entity mentioned in text. Contextualizing information extraction helps to scope the validity of automated finings when aggregating them as knowledge graphs.

arxiv-2503-16308.title: Hamiltonian dynamics of classical spins
arxiv-2503-16308.creator: Slobodan Radošević, Sonja Gombar, Milica Rutonjski, Petar Mali, Milan Pantić, Milica Pavkov-Hrvojević
arxiv-2503-16308.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Slobodan Radošević, Sonja Gombar, Milica Rutonjski, Petar Mali, Milan Pantić, Milica Pavkov-Hrvojević. We discuss the geometry behind classical Heisenberg model at the level suitable for third or fourth year students who did not have the opportunity to take a course on differential geometry. The arguments presented here rely solely on elementary algebraic concepts such as vectors, dual vectors and tensors, as well as Hamiltonian equations and Poisson brackets in their simplest form.

pmc-11542811.title: Competitive plasticity to reduce the energetic costs of learning
pmc-11542811.creator: Mark C. W. van Rossum, Aaron Pache, Daniel Bush, Andrea E. Martin, Daniel Bush, Andrea E. Martin, Daniel Bush, Andrea E. Martin
pmc-11542811.description: The brain is not only constrained by energy needed to fuel computation, but it is also constrained by energy needed to form memories. Experiments have shown that learning simple conditioning tasks which might require only a few synaptic updates, already carries a significant metabolic cost.

pmc-12396136.title: Predicting competitive anion electrosorption on late transition metals
pmc-12396136.creator: Bolton Tran, Bryan R. Goldsmith
pmc-12396136.description: Investigating competitive anion electrosorption on transition metal surfaces is experimentally challenging but critical for advancing electrocatalytic and electrochemical engineering. Here, we present a rigorous computational framework for predicting anion adsorption as a function of the applied potential by combining grand canonical density functional theory (GC-DFT) with thermodynamic cycles.

pmc-12743224.title: Development of Predictive Models for Long-Term Endoscopic Response to Ustekinumab in Crohn’s Disease Based on Plasma Proteomics
pmc-12743224.creator: Chenchen Wu, Jiawen Zheng, Xin Qian, Chunyan Peng, Fan Zhou, Lei Wang
pmc-12743224.description: PurposeUstekinumab (UST) is effective for Crohn’s disease (CD), yet reliable biomarkers for predicting long-term response remain scarce. This study aimed to identify novel plasma proteomic biomarkers and develop predictive models for long-term endoscopic response to UST therapy in patients.MethodsBaseline plasma inflammatory proteins were profiled using the Olink platform in 40 CD patients treated with UST (20 responders, 20 non-responders).

pmc-13202513.title: Cybersecurity and Privacy Issues in Extended Reality Health Care Applications: Scoping Review
pmc-13202513.creator: Kaitlyn Lake, Andrea Mc Kittrick, Mathilde Desselle, Antonio Padilha Lanari Bo, R Achintha M Abayasiri, Jennifer Fleming, Nilufar Baghaei, Dan Dongseong Kim, Tiffany Leung
pmc-13202513.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundVirtual reality (VR) is a type of extended reality (XR) technology that is seeing increasing adoption in health care. There is robust evidence articulating how consumer-grade VR presents significant cybersecurity and privacy risks due to the often ubiquitous and wide range of data collection and user monitoring, as well as the unique user impact of attacks due to the immersive nature of the technology.

pmc-13479665.title: Cement Spacer versus Endoprosthesis as Reconstruction Modality after Limb Salvage for Shoulder Malignancies: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
pmc-13479665.creator: Akshat Gupta, Divesh Jalan, Nishith Gupta, Nupur Aggarwal, Kshitish Behera, Princi Jain
pmc-13479665.description: Background:Limb salvage is the mainstay of surgical treatment for primary sarcomas as well as metastatic lesions of the proximal humerus. This involves wide excision of the involved humeral segment followed by a reconstruction of the defect. The purpose of this review was to determine which reconstruction modality offers a better overall functional outcome.

pmc-13499854.title: The Uptake of Preregistration, and Its Impact on the Proportion of Supported Hypotheses, in Sports Science
pmc-13499854.creator: Hunter Bennett, Henry Blake, Noah d’Unienville, James Murray, Jordan Fox
pmc-13499854.description: BackgroundThe proportion of studies with results supporting their hypotheses has been implausibly high in sports science, suggesting the widespread presence of questionable research practices (QRPs). Preregistration is recommended to mitigate QRPs.ObjectivesThe aim of this study was to evaluate the uptake of preregistration in sports science journals, and its association with the proportion of supported hypotheses.

pmc-13503991.title: Never Say Never: Presumed Inherited Factor VII Deficiency Lies in Wait for 17 Years
pmc-13503991.creator: Austin P Runde, Sofia I Ahmed, Grace C Devitt, Jeremy A Kleberg, Natalie L Kamberos
pmc-13503991.description: A previously healthy, 17-year-old girl presented with gross hematuria in the setting of a severely deranged coagulation profile: prothrombin time (PT) > 320 s, international normalized ratio (INR) 15, and activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) 59 s. Factor VII (F7) activity (FVII:C) was undetectable.

pmc-13652484.title: Successful repair of a penetrating right atrial gunshot injury via right posterolateral thoracotomy in a resource-limited hospital: a case report
pmc-13652484.creator: Issam Alkhayer, Mohammad Alaa Aldakak, Youssef Abbas
pmc-13652484.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background:Penetrating cardiac injuries are uncommon but frequently fatal, particularly after gunshot wounds. Diagnosis may be challenging when pleural bleeding predominates, and pericardial fluid is minimal because blood may decompress through a pericardial defect into the thoracic cavity.Case presentation:A 25-year-old man sustained a penetrating chest gunshot wound during wartime and presented to a resource-limited hospital in hemorrhagic shock with a massive right hemothorax. Right tube thoracostomy immediately drained approximately 900 mL of blood, but he remained hemodynamically unstable.
